title: fix(runtime): refresh atuin init after builds
body:
## Problem

`runtime --build --apply` planned Atuin's Zsh initialization before refreshing and building the repository-owned binary. A first build therefore installed Atuin without generating `_atuin.zsh`, while an upgrade generated the file from the old binary. Dependency skips also stopped at one level, so runtime and planning-time source failures could not safely block a downstream generator.

## Solution

Plan repository-owned source/build operations before generated shell functions and make `function.atuin` depend on the requested `binary.atuin` whenever a fresh build or an existing binary can produce initialization. Propagate dependency-blocked skips, including pre-planned skips caused by a rejected source, so source or build failures preserve the previous binary and initialization as one coherent pair. Keep the existing explicit refresh model, atomic publication, `.zcompdump` handling, and offline behavior unchanged.

## Related

- Amp thread: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019f8e04-1450-7079-af7c-f13ef33e51cf

## Verification

- `mise run test -- tests/test_runtime.py` — 40 passed
- `mise run verify` — 227 behavior tests passed; format, lint, shell, typecheck, and macOS module suites passed
- `mise run runtime -- --build --json` — observed `source.atuin → binary.atuin → function.atuin` on the live checkout
